spec.name: Earnings drift v24
spec.notes: Rank names by the latest earnings surprise and hold through the drift.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.7, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.73 to 2.64 (change -0.10).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.73 to 0.10. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.68 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.73); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.73 against 2.73 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.52 against 2.73 in research, a gap of +2.21.
The best year gives 16% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give 81%; Sharpe is 3.24 in calm and 1.76 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.70 becomes 2.70 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.79 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.00, 95th percentile 0.45).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 20% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 13% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
